svg.desc: Banner for a paper on the stability of plug-and-play iterations with Gaussian kernel denoisers. Left: the exact region of instability of the paper's four-point Gaussian family, plotted from the paper's formula for Δ(ε, t), with the weak-link affinity ε on a logarithmic axis from 10^-8 to 10^-4 and the step size t from 0 to 0.8. Both PnP-ISTA and PnP-ADMM are unstable inside a thin pink region that exists only for ε below about 1.7×10^-5. A dashed curve, the one-parameter family ε = t/100000 used in the main theorem, runs through the region and leaves it at t* ≈ 0.531. Right: along that dashed family, the growth per iteration, ρ(P) − 1, rises from zero to a peak of about 1.7×10^-5 near t = 0.25 and returns to zero at t*. Tenfold growth therefore needs 10^5 to 10^6 iterations, while typical runs use 20 to 500. A footnote names the two proved remedies: scale the step with the mixing gap, or symmetrise the denoiser.
svg.text: Where the four-point Gaussian denoiser fails
exact unstable region Δ(ε, t) < 0 (Theorem 4); weak-link affinity ε against step size t
growth per iteration, ρ(P) − 1, along the dashed family (Section 12)
tenfold growth needs 10⁵–10⁶ iterations; typical runs use 20–500
Remedies proved: scale t with the mixing gap, or symmetrise the denoiser
